status_summary: USAID closed on 2025-07-01, so ADS Chapter 320 and the USAID brand office no longer operate, and the question is whether State carries the outcome. A State official said on 2025-07-02 that State was consolidating the logos of its offices, embassies, bureaus and programs, including those formerly under USAID, into a single flag-based logo with compliance due 2025-10-01; the report does not say whether implementing partners must use it. H.R. 7633 (American Assistance Visibility Act), introduced 2026-02-20, would amend the Foreign Assistance Act to make the US flag the sole visual brand on tangible foreign assistance items, subject to exceptions and waivers, with State regulations; the House Foreign Affairs Committee ordered it reported on 2026-03-26, and no floor action was found. No new rule enforcing marking on all grants, cooperative agreements and contracts, appointee brand adviser or USAGM coordination was found, so the stage rests on the operative logo change and is held at the bottom of the in_progress band.

timeline.event: USAID officially closed and its remaining operations merged into State.

A State official told Fox News that State offices, embassies, bureaus and programs, including those formerly under USAID, would be consolidated under a single flag-based logo, with compliance due by 2025-10-01.

H.R. 7633, the American Assistance Visibility Act, was introduced and referred to the House Foreign Affairs Committee; it would add a section 641A to the Foreign Assistance Act requiring the US flag as the sole visual brand on foreign assistance items, with exceptions, a security waiver and State regulations.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee marked up H.R. 7633 and ordered it reported in the nature of a substitute by a recorded vote of 44 to 1 (GovInfo bill status); CBO also states the committee ordered it reported on that date.
CBO issued a cost estimate for H.R. 7633, describing a requirement to display the US flag on foreign assistance and a rulemaking duty for the Secretary of State.

title: Enforce US branding on all foreign aid and credit the American people
uncertainties: The Fox report relays a State official's description of a logo consolidation for State offices, embassies, bureaus and programs and does not say whether implementing partners must use the new brand; no State guidance document was read. The Foreign Affairs Manual page shows 2018 dates and says USAID programs had separate rules, so it shows only that State partner-marking rules existed before 2025. The 2020 branding order was revoked by Executive Order 14029 in May 2021; no 2025 or 2026 order replacing it was found. Bill introduction and text were confirmed on GovInfo and the committee markup on the House committee repository; congress.gov could not be read, and the 44 to 1 committee tally is confirmed by GovInfo BILLSTATUS, which on 2026-10-24 listed 2026-03-26 as the latest action (record updated 2026-09-10). The bill covers tangible items and outreach products and does not name grants, contracts or cooperative agreements. FY2026 appropriations branding provisions were searched in committee summaries and a CRS report, and none was found. Searches found nothing on a Senior Advisor for Brand Management or on Agency for Global Media coordination. The stage is a judgment call: the logo change is operative but may cover only State's own branding, so proposed 20 on the bill alone is the alternative. A House Rules Committee amendment submission attributed to Rep. Shreve and dated 2026-06-22 (to Rules Committee Print 119-33) would add the same section 641A and apply flag rules to implementing partners; it was not opened by the reviewer, and whether it was made in order or adopted was not found. No State Department branding rule or guidance after April 2026 and no related Federal Register document were found, and the primary State document behind the 2025 logo report was not located.
